output:
To: @marco
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Desert Palms — codes and tray

Marco,

I’m pissed about how you left the Desert Palms job. You told me Saturday the 14 units were done and the keys were with Yvette, but not one code made it into the sheet. Now she needs three copies for 9B today, and I’ve got nothing to cut from. Lupe also found your pinning tray, with pins still in it, sitting on the leasing office counter. That’s not how we leave a job.

This is the same problem as Kessler in September. I told you then, and in August I put the rule out to everybody: every rekey and master job gets its bitting codes in the sheet the same day, before you leave the van. Address, unit, code. No exceptions. It’s not optional, and I’m not going to keep chasing you for work records after the fact.

Go back to Desert Palms today and decode 9B at a minimum so we can get Yvette those copies. If you can recover and document the codes for all 14 units, do that too. Put them in the sheet with the right unit numbers, then bring my pinning tray back to the shop. Make sure it’s complete and the pins are accounted for.

I’m not saying this to pick a fight, and I’m not firing you. You’re good with your hands and I value the work you do. But this can’t keep happening. The codes matter for the next call, and leaving tools behind at a customer’s office is careless. I need you to take care of both things today and make the same-day code entry part of how you finish every job from now on. Tell me when it’s done.

reasons: The draft says Lupe found the pinning tray, but Yvette reported it and Lupe only relayed the call.
